# DC wiki codec — segmenting MD→wiki render behind WikiTextCodec (capability only)

## Context / Problem
Jira Data Center stores rich text as wiki markup (REST v2), a lossy text format.
The `RichTextCodec` seam (epic `e369`, story J3 / `aac8`) routes DC rich text
through **`WikiTextCodec`** (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:72`), today an
**identity** codec: `fit_outbound` (`:82`), `normalize_outbound` (`:96`), `to_wire`
(`:100`), `decode_inbound` (`:104`) all pass the plain string through. So DC ships
rebar's raw Markdown as literal wiki source.

No library round-trips rebar's punctuation-dense prose: pandoc's jira reader
misparses `->`, ASCII pipe-tables, and regex, and provably erodes them one
character per pass (the ASCII-table body decays 9115→9110 monotonically). A
whole-body all-or-nothing conversion is echo-safe but only ~15% rich. A
**segmenting** one-way renderer that converts only structurally-safe units and
passes dangerous ones through verbatim reaches ~68% of bodies / ~78% of chars
rich, proven non-corrupting across 23 environments, 6 authors, and an
out-of-distribution corpus.

**Scope boundary (why this story changes nothing observable yet).** The live DC
outbound send does **not** yet apply a non-identity codec: descriptions are
composed by the SHARED `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote` at
`adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:77`
(`normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))`) → `_issues.py:44 update_issue` →
`issue.update(fields=…)`, and the DC CREATE path builds the description via
`codec.fit_outbound` at `backend.py:70`. This story delivers only the **codec
capability** — a `WikiTextCodec` whose `to_wire` renders MD→wiki and whose four
ops satisfy the codec law — plus its unit/corpus tests. **Wiring the live DC send
and CREATE path to the rendered wire, proving second-pass convergence, and the
rollback path are owned by the echo-safety story `3388`, which depends on this
one.** This ordering is deliberate: `3388` carries the state-based echo
suppression, so the lossy render must not go live before it. Until `3388` wires
it, `WikiTextCodec` is capable but the live send still ships today's identity
output.

## Prior art in this repo (the seam we build on — NOT greenfield)
- `WikiTextCodec` (DC) — `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:72`, identity today;
  constructed into the shared `OutboundFieldMapper` at `backend.py:84`.
- `RichTextCodec` Protocol — four ops; the wire op is `to_wire` (DC: a wiki `str`).
  The intended composition `to_wire(normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(text)))` is
  proven in `test_rich_text_codec.py:53`.
- **Codec law (ticket a32a):** `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`
  is parametrized in `test_rich_text_codec.py:163`
  (`test_normalize_outbound_equals_decode_of_to_wire`). It is **load-bearing**: the
  comment differ's dedup (`outbound_comments.py:48`, `_diff_comments` with an
  injected codec) documents that symmetric degradation depends on this law. A
  codec whose `to_wire` renders while `normalize_outbound` stays identity **breaks
  the law**, so this story keeps all four ops consistent (below).
- **Guard:** `backend.py:131 normalize_rich_text` is the **INBOUND** decode and
  delegates to the SHARED plain-text `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` (ticket
  21ca; also used by sibling repo `agentic-dev-platform`) — it is NOT the outbound
  render seam and is left unchanged.
- **Import contract (ADR 0035):** `jira_family/` must not import `adapters/jira/`.
  pandoc/`pypandoc` is not a Cloud module, so the renderer lives in `jira_family/`.

## Approach (capability, behind the seam)
Implement the segmenting renderer as **`WikiTextCodec.to_wire`** (delegating to a
new `wiki_render.py` module to respect the module-size cap), and make the four ops
codec-law-consistent:
- `to_wire(t)` = segmenting MD→wiki render (below).
- `decode_inbound(w)` = the existing inbound read (identity/plain today) — DC does
  not parse wiki back to Markdown, so decode stays the read-as-is transform.
- `normalize_outbound(t)` = **`decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` by construction** (no
  longer identity), so the codec law holds for the rendered wire. This is the
  compare form the description differ and comment dedup use.
- `fit_outbound` = unchanged character-budget fit.

Pipeline (`wiki_render.py`): split the body into blocks and list-items; render
structurally-safe units (headings, lists, code, quotes, safe paragraphs) to wiki
via pinned `pandoc` (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`); pass dangerous units
(ASCII tables, arrow/regex/HTML-dense prose) through **verbatim**; reassemble in
original order. Two lossless render rules: **code-aware arrow substitution**
(`-> <- <-> =>` → `→ ← ↔ ⇒`, prose-only, skipping fenced/inline code) which MUST
run on the **Markdown before pandoc**; and **verbatim-wrapping ASCII tables in
`{noformat}`** to stop per-pass dash erosion.

**pandoc delivery (portability).** Pin **`pypandoc-binary`** (bundles a pandoc
binary in the wheel) rather than bare `pypandoc` (which requires a system pandoc)
so the DC path is self-contained in CI and prod. At codec construction, probe
pandoc availability once; if pandoc is **absent or errors**, `to_wire` **falls
back to identity passthrough** (today's behavior — echo-safe, never corrupting),
logs once, and the codec law still holds (`normalize_outbound` = identity of
`to_wire` = identity). GPL/SBOM compliance for the bundled binary is handled by
the robustness story `5c0e`.

## Explicitly OUT of scope for this story (owned by `3388`)
- Wiring `to_wire` into the live DC send (`outbound_mapper.py:77`) and the CREATE
  path (`backend.py:70`) — the observable wire cutover.
- The second-pass DC convergence proof (a repeated pass emits zero description
  updates) and the rollback path.
This story leaves `outbound_mapper.py:77` and `backend.py:70` untouched, so no
observable DC behavior changes on merge.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` — `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` delegates to the
  renderer; `normalize_outbound` set to `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (law-consistent).
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (new) — segmenting renderer (split →
  per-unit safe-render/passthrough → reassemble; arrow substitution; table wrap;
  pandoc-availability probe + identity fallback). ADR-0035-clean.
- `pyproject.toml` — pinned `pypandoc-binary` extra.
- **Guard (UNCHANGED):** `backend.py:131 normalize_rich_text` (inbound, shared);
  the live send sites `outbound_mapper.py:77` and `backend.py:70` (wired by `3388`).
- `tests/` — segmenting/arrow/table/law corpus tests.

## Testing (unit + corpus only — no live send in this story)
- Happy path: headings + a checklist + a fenced code block render to wiki
  `h1.`/`*`-bullets/`{code}` via `to_wire` and reassemble in original order.
- Danger passthrough: an ASCII pipe-table, a prose `->`, and a `obj->method()`
  code arrow render with the table verbatim in `{noformat}`, prose `->`→`→`, and
  the code arrow untouched.
- **Codec law:** `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` holds for
  DC wiki fixtures; verified by the parametrized `test_rich_text_codec.py:163`
  extended with the DC codec.
- **pandoc-absent fallback:** with pandoc unavailable, `to_wire` returns the input
  unchanged (identity), the law still holds, and a warning is logged once
  (`test_dc_pandoc_absent_falls_back_to_identity`).
- Corpus coverage/safety: over the historical corpus the renderer yields rich for
  ~68% of bodies with 0 code-arrow rewrites and 0 prose corruptions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` segments a body and renders only structurally-safe
  units, passing dangerous units (tables/arrows/regex/HTML) verbatim; verified by
  `test_dc_segmenting_passthrough` on a mixed body.
- [ ] `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (the
  codec law) holds with the rendering `to_wire`; verified by
  `test_rich_text_codec.py:163` extended with the DC codec.
- [ ] Code-aware arrow substitution runs on the Markdown before pandoc and touches
  0 code arrows; verified by a test asserting `obj->method()` is unchanged while a
  prose `->` becomes `→` (regression over the 179 known code-arrow bodies: 0
  rewrites).
- [ ] ASCII tables are verbatim-wrapped in `{noformat}` and do not erode across
  passes; verified by `test_dc_table_noformat_stable` over the known erosion
  bodies (70/70 stable).
- [ ] `pypandoc-binary` is pinned and, when pandoc is unavailable, `to_wire` falls
  back to identity passthrough (echo-safe) with the law preserved; verified by
  `test_dc_pandoc_absent_falls_back_to_identity`.
- [ ] Over the historical corpus the renderer produces rich output for ≈68% of
  bodies / ≈78% of chars with zero prose corruption; verified by
  `test_dc_corpus_coverage`.
- [ ] The shared inbound `normalize_rich_text` and the live send sites
  (`outbound_mapper.py:77`, `backend.py:70`) are unchanged by this story; verified
  by their existing tests staying green (the observable cutover is `3388`).
